'''Derrick JaVaughn Byars''' (born April 25, 1984) is an American entrepreneur and former professional [[basketball]] player. Collegiately, he played for [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], and later for [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]]. He was drafted 42nd overall in the [[2007 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
Byars attended [[Ridgeway High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Ridgeway High School]] in Memphis, where he played for head coach Wesley Henning and won two [[Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association]] ([[TSSAA]]) Class AA State Championships.

As a [[wiktionary:sophomore|sophomore]] (1999–2000), Byars was an honorable-mention All-State selection and led the Roadrunners to the Class AA State Championship. He averaged 16.4 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 6.5 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 5.4 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] per game.

As a [[Eleventh grade|junior]], he again earned honorable mention All-State honors and was named Ridgeway's Most Valuable Player and District 15-AA MVP. He averaged 20.5 points, 7.2 rebounds and 5 assists.

As a [[Twelfth grade|senior]] (2001–02), he averaged 23.2 points, 10 rebounds and 4.5 assists and led Ridgeway to its second TSSAA Class AA State Championship in three years. He was a fourth-team [[All-America#High school sports|Parade All-America]] selection, the Gatorade Player of the Year in Tennessee, the TSSAA Class AA Tournament Most Valuable Player and first-team All-State.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://virginiasports.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/byars_derrick00.html|title=Derrick Byars Profile (Virginia)|publisher=CSTV.com|access-date = March 8, 2007}}</ref>

Byars also excelled in the classroom, finishing [[high school]] with a 3.9 [[Grading in education|GPA]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cavalierdaily.com/news/2002/nov/12/derrick-byars/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120721233225/http://www.cavalierdaily.com/news/2002/nov/12/derrick-byars/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 21, 2012 |title=Derrick Byars Inside Out |work=[[Cavalier Daily]] |date=November 12, 2002 |last=Moss |first=J.D. |access-date=March 8, 2007 }}</ref>

==Collegiate career==

===Virginia===
Byars played for two seasons under then-head coach [[Pete Gillen]] at [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]]. He started 16 of Virginia's 31 games his freshman season (2002–03) and averaged 6.5 points per game. In his sophomore season (2003–04), he started 18 of Virginia's 31 games and averaged 7.5 points per game.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://vucommodores.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/byars_derrick00.html|title=Derrick Byars Profile (Vanderbilt)|publisher=CSTV.com|access-date = March 8, 2007}}</ref>

Disappointed by his lack of playing time, Byars decided to transfer from Virginia.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=1836602 Byars comes from UVa as transfer - Men's College Basketball - ESPN]</ref> Vanderbilt emerged as a leading candidate due to Byars' friendships with players on the team and the Commodores' recent run to the Sweet 16 of the [[2004 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.vandypride.com/2008/06/02/catching-up-with-derrick-byars/ |title=Archived copy |access-date=April 5, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130408014342/http://www.vandypride.com/2008/06/02/catching-up-with-derrick-byars/ |archive-date=April 8, 2013 }}</ref> but the Commodores had no scholarship positions available. Days before Byars was due to announce his transfer to [[University of Mississippi|Mississippi]], Vanderbilt reserve guard Adam Payton decided to transfer to [[College of William & Mary|William & Mary]], freeing up a scholarship for Byars.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/03/19/sports/ncaabasketball/19vandy.html|title=Commodores' Success Is Built on Two Players Who Never Met|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date = March 19, 2007 | first=Lee | last=Jenkins | date=March 19, 2007}}</ref>

He sat out the 2004–05 season as mandated by NCAA rules.

===Vanderbilt===
In his junior season (2005–06), Byars started all 30 games and finished second on the team in scoring at 12.4 points per game. He started a handful of games at the point guard position and led the team with 3.2 assists per game. He was named SEC Player of the Week (November 28 – December 4) after scoring 20 points on 7-of-8 shooting against [[Oregon Ducks|Oregon]] on November 30, 2005. A week later, he scored a season-high 25 points (including five 3-pointers) against [[Cincinnati Bearcats|Cincinnati]] on December 10, 2005.<ref name="cstv.com">{{cite web |url=http://vucommodores.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/byars_derrick00.html|title=Derrick Byars Profile 2006–07|publisher=CSTV.com|access-date = March 8, 2007}}</ref>

In his senior season (2006–07), Byars was named [[Southeastern Conference]] Player of the Year by the league's coaches, who also unanimously selected him to their All-SEC first team. He led Vanderbilt to a 22–12 record ([[Southeastern Conference|SEC East]]: 10–6, 2nd) and the {{strike|Elite Eight}} Sweet 16 of the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]], because Jeff Green's travel was not called, ending the season at least one game early. He led the Commodores in scoring with 17.0 points per game and was ranked among the SEC's top 10 in four other statistical categories. During SEC play, Byars averaged 19.1 points per game, second-best in the SEC. He scored 20 points or more eight different times, including a career-high 32 points against [[South Carolina Gamecocks|South Carolina]] on February 14, 2007. He followed that performance with 24 points in Vanderbilt's 83–70 victory over then-No. 1 [[Florida Gators|Florida]], which earned him SEC player of the week honors for the second time that season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tennessean.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20070308/SPORTS0602/703080416/1002|title=Coaches say Byars SEC's best|publisher=Tennessean.com |access-date = March 8, 2007}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>

Byars graduated from Vanderbilt on May 11, 2007, with a degree in sociology.

==Professional career==

===NBA===
Byars was chosen 42nd overall in the [[2007 NBA draft]] in the second round by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. His rights were then traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tennessean.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=2007705090445|title=Byars may go late in first round|publisher=Tennessean.com|access-date = May 14, 2007}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref> He was waived by the 76ers on October 22, 2007. He was on the [[New Orleans Hornets]] and [[Orlando Magic]] rosters for the 2008 Summer League.  Byars return to the NBA Summer League was successful, as he led the Magic in scoring in their first game against the New Jersey Nets with 15 points on 6 of 13 shooting [https://web.archive.org/web/20081013145936/http://www.nba.com/media/magic/Game_3_Box_Score.pdf].

In late September, Byars was signed by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] where he averaged 4.1 points and 14.8 minutes per game in the preseason.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tulsaworld.com/sports/article.aspx?articleID=20080930_226_B5_OKLAHO809612|title= Thunder Notebook|access-date=September 30, 2008|publisher= Tulsa World |date=September 30, 2008}}</ref>

Byars was invited to the [[Chicago Bulls]]' training camp in 2009 but was waived on the opening day of the season, October 28, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagobreakingsports.com/2009/10/bulls-starting-5.html |title=Bulls' starting 5?  |access-date=October 28, 2008 |publisher= Chicago Breaking Sports News |date=October 28, 2008 }}</ref>

He played for the Bulls in the [[NBA Summer League]] in 2010.<ref>[http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/6/28/1540775/nba-summer-league-rosters-vegas NBA Summer League Rosters - Vegas]</ref>

===Germany===
In December 2007, Byars played in eight games for the [[Köln 99ers]], a [[Basketball Bundesliga]] team based in [[Cologne]], Germany, having arrived at the end of October with a foot injury that had to be cured first. He averaged 6.3 points and 18 minutes per game in four games in the [[ULEB Cup]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?clubcode=col&pcode=000685&seasoncode=u2007|title=Derrick Byars – Köln 99ers Game Log|publisher=Euroleague.net|access-date = January 22, 2008}}</ref> and 3.5 points in another 4 games in the Bundesliga. He was cut from the team again on December 21, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.koeln99ers.de/99ers/index3.php?cat=news&storyID=466 |title=Köln 99ers trennen sich von Derrick Byars (Köln 99ers are separating from Derrick Byars) |language=de |publisher=Köln 99ers Official Homepage |access-date=March 6, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071231125543/http://www.koeln99ers.de/99ers/index3.php?cat=news&storyID=466 |archive-date=December 31, 2007 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On November 2, 2009, Byars was introduced as the new small forward for [[ALBA Berlin]].

===France===
On January 24, 2008, he was subsequently signed by [[Chorale Roanne Basket]] of the [[Ligue Nationale de Basketball]] (LNB) in France.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/team.asp?Cntry=FRA&Team=417|title=Chorale Roanne Basket Current Roster|publisher=Eurobasket.com|access-date = March 6, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chorale-roanne.com/?id=1&num=1475|title=Derrick Byars est choralien (Derrick Byars is a Choralien)|language=fr|publisher=Chorale Roanne Official Homepage|access-date = March 6, 2008}}</ref>

His club finished fourth in the 2007/08 regular season, and lost in the 2008 LNB final against [[SLUC Nancy|Nancy]] after beating regular season winner Le Mans in the semi-final. 
Byars averaged 8 points and 3 rebounds in 24 minutes of playing time.<ref>[http://www.lnb.fr/index.php?pid=9&id=A41010&from=2007&type=1 Ligue Nationale de Basket<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

===NBA Development League===
Derrick Byars was drafted in the [[2008 NBA Development League draft]] with the 5th overall pick by the [[Bakersfield Jam]]. While averaging 18 points per game on the season, he was named to the 2009 NBA D-League All-Star Game and led all players in scoring with 18 points. He returned to the team briefly in 2011, claiming another NBA Developmental League Player of the Week award after scoring a career-high 45 points versus Springfield Armor.

===Greece===
In September 2010, he signed a one-year deal with the [[HEBA A1 Ethniki|Greek]] club [[Panellinios Basket]].<ref>[http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/on-court/transactions/eurocup-2010-11/i/75588/4674/panellinios-signs-derrick-byars PANELLINIOS signs Derrick Byars.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100926122841/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/on-court/transactions/eurocup-2010-11/i/75588/4674/panellinios-signs-derrick-byars |date=September 26, 2010 }}</ref>

===Return to France===
In August 2011 he signed a one-year contract with [[Cholet Basket]] in France.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/86995/180/cholet-basket-signs-byars Cholet Basket signs Byars]</ref> However, he left the club in November, having played only two games, one in [[2011–12 LNB season|Pro A]] and one in the [[Euroleague 2011–12 qualifying rounds|Euroleague qualifying round]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cholet-basket.com/news/actualites/derrick-byars-quitte-cholet-basket-n5104.htm |title=Derrick Byars quitte Cholet |publisher=cholet-basket.com |date=November 12, 2011 |language=fr |access-date=November 12, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160119142457/http://www.cholet-basket.com/news/actualites/derrick-byars-quitte-cholet-basket-n5104.htm |archive-date=January 19, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Return to the NBA===
On December 10, 2011, Byars signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_signs_derrick_byars_111210.html HEAT Signs Derrick Byars]</ref> He was however waived before the start of the season. He was then signed by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on April 25, 2012.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120425_sign_derrick_byars Spurs Sign Derrick Byars]</ref> On August 21, 2012, he was waived by the Spurs after scoring ten points in two games.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120821_spurs_waive_derrick_byars Spurs Waive Derrick Byars]</ref>

===Return to Germany===
In November 2012, Byars re-signed with Alba Berlin.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/103736/180/alba-berlin-brings-back-byars  Alba Berlin brings back Byars]</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies===
In September 2013, Byars joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/09/grizzlies-sign-byars-ely-gaffney.html Grizzlies Sign Byars, Ely, Gaffney]</ref> He was waived by the team on October 6, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14444 |title=Memphis Grizzlies waive Josh Akognon and Derrick Byars |access-date=October 7, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150610205327/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14444 |archive-date=June 10, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Russia / D-League===
In January 2014, Byars signed with BC Krasny Oktyabr of Russia for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/110443/derrick-byars-to-sign-deal-with-krasny-oktyabr.html Derrick Byars To Sign Deal With Krasny Oktyabr]</ref> He left before playing in a game for them.

On March 4, 2014, he was re-acquired by the Bakersfield Jam.

===Belgium===
On April 12, 2014, Byars signed with [[Belfius Mons-Hainaut]] of the [[Basketball League Belgium Division I|Basketball League Belgium]] for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/belgium/116929/derrick-byars-signs-with-mons.html |title=Derrick Byars signs with Mons |access-date=April 30, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502013302/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/belgium/116929/derrick-byars-signs-with-mons.html |archive-date=May 2, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

===Israel===
On September 15, 2015, Byars signed with [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]] from the [[Israel Basketball Super League|Israel Super League]].<ref name="roster">[http://www.maccabirishon.co.il/%D7%91%D7%9C%D7%95%D7%92/873/ The roster is complete] {{in lang|he}}</ref><ref name="Rishon">[http://basket.co.il/News.asp?id=6096 Derrick Byars signed with Rishon LeZion] {{in lang|he}}</ref>

===Puerto Rico===
On January 6, 2016, Byars signed with [[Santeros de Aguada]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>[http://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/detalles.asp?r=9925 Aguada firma a Derrick Byars]</ref>

===France===
On August 20, 2016, Byars signed with [[JA Vichy]] of the [[LNB Pro B]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vcm-basket.com/fr/Actualites-du-club/Derrick-byars-evoluera-avec-la-javcm---ac301|title=Derrick BYARS évoluera avec la J.A.VCM|work=vcm-basket.com|date=August 20, 2016|access-date=February 28, 2017}}</ref> In 16 games, he averaged 12 points, five rebounds, two assists and one steal.<ref name="Sevens">{{cite web|url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/sevens-acquire-derrick-byars/|title=SEVENS ACQUIRE DERRICK BYARS|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2017|access-date=February 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170228003043/http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/sevens-acquire-derrick-byars/|archive-date=February 28, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===D-League===
On February 27, 2017, he was acquired by the [[Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref name="Sevens"/>
